title: Hybrid preemptible quant-batching playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for sizing and operating a hybrid fleet that mixes dedicated GPUs with preemptible/spot capacity while using low-bit quantization and adaptive batching. Goal: maximize effective tokens/sec per dollar while keeping p95 latency < 350ms and a monitored "quality anchor" delta < 2% on key eval prompts.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Hybrid strategy lets us absorb short bursts and reduce committed capacity, but preemptible churn interacts badly with large KV caches and long-lived sessions.
- Quantization to 8-bit yields ~2.6x tokens/sec per GPU vs fp16 with ~=1.5% quality drop on our eval set; 4-bit pushes to ~3.8x but quality delta grows non-linear beyond 3.5%.
- Priority-aware batching (separate high-priority low-latency lane) and pre-warming KV caches for pinned customers keeps p95 tail in check.
- Recommended operational modes: Balanced Hybrid (baseline), Spot-Burst (cost-optimized with more reserved fallback) and Conservative Core (low-cost savings, high SLA). See scenarios below.

Assumptions and inputs (what went into numbers):
- GPU types tested: H100 (dedicated), A100-SXM (reserved), T4-like preemptible used for low-precision only.
- Workload mix: 65% short requests (<64 tokens), 25% medium (64-256 tokens), 10% long (>256 tokens).
- Latency target: median < 120ms, p95 < 350ms.
- Quality anchor: evaluation corpus of 250 prompts representing our high-value routes. Metric = mean normalized human-score proxy (0-100). Baseline (fp16) = 100.

Simulation matrix (representative snapshot from local sim):
Scenario | Fleet mix (dedicated:spot) | Quant profile | Effective tok/s per GPU | median ms | p95 ms | quality delta
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Conservative Core | 90:10 | fp16 default | 120K | 110 | 280 | 0%
Balanced Hybrid | 70:30 | mixed (fp16 + 8-bit) | 210K | 125 | 320 | -1.6%
Spot-Burst | 40:60 | 8-bit heavy + 4-bit for stateless | 260K | 145 | 470 | -3.8%
Fallback-First | 60:40 | 8-bit, auto-fallback to fp16 on high-error | 190K | 135 | 305 | -0.9%

Notes on the table: effective tokens/sec is end-to-end observed throughput accounting for batching inefficiencies and preemption restart overheads. Spot-Burst p95 is high due to cache churn and requeueing on preemption.

Operational heuristics (how to run):
1) Split routing into lanes:
   - Latency lane (high-priority): only dedicated GPUs, conservative quant (fp16/8-bit with cache warm).
   - Cost lane (best-effort): preemptible + aggressive quant (8-bit/4-bit) with shorter seq-length thresholds.
2) KV cache anchoring: reserve a small dedicated pool for customers with pinned sessions to avoid cold-cache p95 spikes.
3) Graceful fallback: if quality anchor for a model variant drifts > 2% for 5 consecutive eval windows, automatically route that customer to a verified fp16 variant.
4) Preemption handling: proactively checkpoint KV state every N requests (N configurable by route) for stateless-friendly models; for stateful sessions, prefer reserved capacity.
5) Autoscaling policy: use predictive scaling (windowed SMA of incoming qps + burst buffer) rather than purely reactive to minimize cold-starts.

Cost sensitivity and decision boundaries:
- If spot availability > 60% and preemption rate < 8% -> favor Spot-Burst for non-critical customers.
- If spot preemptions trending upward 2-week rolling avg -> shift 10% capacity from spot to dedicated to protect tail SLOs.
- Quality delta > 2% on anchor prompts -> reduce aggressive quantization, increase fallback ratio to dedicated by +15% until anchor recovers.

Monitoring signals (what to track live):
- Quality anchor score (per-customer and fleet-wide) on rolling 30-min windows.
- Preemption rate (per-region, per-instance type).
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction rate.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU class and per-queue.
- p50/p95/p99 latencies broken down by route and batch-size.
- Model output regression alerts tied to specific prompt subsets.

Open questions / risks:
- Long-lived chat sessions (heavy KV growth) on spot instances: do we permit graceful migration or force session pinning? (Action: engineering to prototype live-migration of KV shards — JIRA-INFRA-3012)
- Quant quality non-uniformity across languages: initial tests show Spanish prompts degrade ~1.2x more on 4-bit. Need language-aware quant profiles.
- Legal/regulatory customers cannot use preemptible; ensure routing metadata prevents accidental placement.

Quick runbook (incidents involving spot churn causing p95 spikes):
- Pager triggers on p95 > 400ms for > 5m across >3 routes.
- Ops steps:
  1) Flip cost-lane to fallback-first (directive in routing service) to move 25% of in-flight requests to dedicated.
  2) Increase batch timeout on spot nodes by +5ms to improve packing while controlling latency regressions.
  3) If quality anchor drops > 3%, enable model-level fallback to validated fp16 variants.

Testing and validation plan:
- A/B run for 4 weeks: baseline (Conservative Core) vs Balanced Hybrid on low-value routes; track unit economics, p95, and anchor.
- Offline eval: expand anchor prompt set to 1k examples with language slices (EN, ES, FR) and content types (code, conversation, doc summarization).
- Chaos-testing: scheduled preemption storms in us-west region to validate checkpoint and migration behavior.

Appendix: short experiment logs (notes)
- 2029-08-15 Miguel: Spot preemption spike coincided with cache eviction policy change; rebalanced policy and reduced p95 by 80ms.
- 2029-08-22 Priya: 4-bit + KV compression experiment reduced DRAM by 30% but increased generation artefacts on completions >512 tokens.
- 2029-08-30 James: predictive scaler tuned with 6-min lookahead cut cold-start events by 63%.

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype KV live-migration (owner: Miguel, JIRA-INFRA-3012) — due 2029-10-02
- Add language-aware quant profiles to model catalog (owner: Priya) — due 2029-09-20
- Run 4-week A/B (owner: Aisha) — kickoff 2029-09-10
